text:
maya: Quick follow-up on RFC #312 about extracting runtime submodules. I sketched some practical guardrails so we don't end up with half-broken services after the cutover. TL;DR: contract-first, small slices, observable by default, and explicit ownership handoff.

jon: +1. Can you list the must-haves for a slice to be 'extraction-ready'?

maya: Sure — thinking baseline checklist:
- backward-compatible API surface (semver-ish)
- clear data ownership for KV/cache prefixes
- perf & cost targets for the slice (p999, tokens/sec)
- CI & e2e that run against both old and new at once
- rollout story (canary, shadowing, feature-flagged cut)

sam: Also add "telemetry tags" required for SLOs. If we lose trace continuity during extraction it's a non-starter.

helen: For API compatibility, do we want a strict contract format? e.g., proto/jsonschema with example responses?

maya: Yes — contract artifacts as first-class: small OpenAPI snippet + a compatibility test. Example minimal contract: ```json
{
  "paths": {
    "/v1/session/{id}": {
      "get": {
        "responses": {"200": {"content": {"application/json": {}}}}
      }
    }
  }
}
```
This enforces shape and required fields.

raj: How do we handle prefix-based KV ownership? Some slices read many prefixes owned by core. Cutting read-only first and write-later?

maya: Strategy: read-routing variant first (new service reads from core), then write-proxying for a transition window, finally cutover writes. Must have a durable migration log for ops.

jon: Migration log = an append-only table showing keys and epochs? We need to ensure monotonicity for replay.

sam: We should also require idempotency for any operation that will be replayed during migration. Documented retry semantics.

helen: Testing: we want smoke tests that run against both runtime and extracted service in CI. How heavy should those be?

maya: Keep them fast (10-20s), exercise the contract surface and critical paths (signing, kv read/write, caching behaviors). Heavy perf tests run in a separate pipeline nightly.

raj: Observability guardrail: new service must emit trace-parent and token_count tags, and inherit request_id from gateway. No exceptions.

sam: Ops requirement: each extracted service needs runbook + rollback recipe checked into repo before merge. Also a staging canary window metric threshold (e.g., error rate <0.5%, tail latency delta <10%).

maya: Exactly. I'm also proposing a migration stance matrix so teams know when to pause/rollback:
- Green: pass smoke + metrics within thresholds — proceed canary
- Amber: minor regressions (tail + cost) — extend shadowing, run perf tuning
- Red: correctness or stability failures — immediate rollback and postmortem

jon: One practical question: how big should a slice be? Service-per-model? Service-per-responsibility?

maya: Prefer "bounded capability" — small feature verticals (session management, kv-store, routing). Avoid slicing by infra layer. Keep slices coarse enough to own a business responsibility but small enough to be rewound in one sprint.

helen: Ownership handoff: define which team owns the contract and which team owns the implementation for the migration window. Maybe a simple annotation in the repo: `OWNERS: contract-team, impl-team`

sam: Could also include an "extraction-issue" label template that enforces the checklist fields before merging.

raj: Deployment topology — do we require the extracted service to be able to run in both Dedicated and Hosted modes? That's a lot of extra work for teams.

maya: Not required initially. Must be deployable to our internal staging infra. If it's customer-facing or needs isolation we gate Dedicated certification later. Keep initial bar lower but strict on observability and contract.

jon: Can we automate any of the checklist? e.g., contract compat tests as part of CI, telemetry linting, runbook template generation?

maya: Yes — that's part of the proposal: small infra helpers in devex: `extract-check` CLI that validates contract, generates smoke tests scaffold, and runs telemetry linters. Output should be a single PR artifact that reviewers can eyeball.

infra-bot: [ci] extract-check passed for branch feat/subsystem-split-1724 — 3 checks, 0 failures.

helen: Timeline: propose we treat this as an ongoing capability — pilot with session and routing slices over Q2. Set up an "extraction guild" to help teams for the first 6 months.

sam: Need to surface cost implications up-front. New services add CPU/RAM and possibly multiply KV reads. Add a cost-estimate step in the checklist.

maya: Good call. I'll include a lightweight cost-estimator in the `extract-check` that projects incremental tokens/sec cost and KV RPS.

jon: One more: compatibility table for SDKs. If we move session endpoints, SDKs must support both old and new hosts during migration. Who owns SDK updates?

maya: SDK updates are the contract-owner's responsibility. Contract must include deprecation schedule and migration timeline.

raj: After cutover, how do we handle data cleanup? Will core keep tombstones?

maya: Define retention windows per slice. Default: 7 days of tombstone and a cleanup job that requires approval. Include this in runbook.

helen: Sounds thorough. Next step: turn this into a short RFC appendix with the checklist and the `extract-check` CLI proto. Want me to draft?

maya: Yes please. Draft goal: 1 page checklist + 1 page automation plan. Tagging @jon @sam to review.

sam: I'll review this afternoon. :thumbsup:

jon: I'll add a sample compatibility test to the repo and link in the RFC.

infra-bot: [deploy] scheduled: extraction-guild-weekly at 2026-05-12T16:00:00Z (reminder will post in #general).

maya: Thanks everyone — will circulate draft in the morning.
